column5: A SetFileTime through one hard-link name updates the FILE'S OWN RECORD for every name at once; each name's index entry is a cache the driver refreshes only for the name that was opened, so divergence is evidence, agreement clears nothing (a read produces it too), and which name is authentic is not established.
Do not name an authentic birth from the sibling set; the mechanism behind the observed divergence was never decompiled.
The tool flags EVERY name of a diverging group; flagging only one would assert the others are clean.

A name-scoped SetFileTime updates the FILE'S OWN RECORD for every name at once, so it is not itself the cause of a divergence. What diverges is each NAME'S INDEX ENTRY, a lazily refreshed cache: RefsUpdateFileDupInfo refreshes only the opened name's entry, so an un-opened sibling keeps pre-stomp times and any read erases them. Divergence is evidence; agreement clears nothing; which name is authentic is still not established.
A sparse hole is identified by flags bit 0x20; a hole's VLCN mirrors its file VCN and is usually non-zero. VLCN 0 is only a read-time floor.
A checksummed extent carries one CRC-32C per cluster and declares it in record size (24 + run*4); 0x1C00D0 is flags 0x00D0 with record size 28, i.e. run == 1 only.
A redo block's record budget is its own total_size; first_record_offset only locates the first record.
The last record of a redo block carries the commit flag (bit 1 at +0x2C) on every block measured.
Bytes per sector is 512 on a 512e volume and 4096 on a 4Kn one; total_sectors counts sectors of that size.
The carves 1.13.0 refused were genuine: 86 of 93 with a live twin are byte-identical to it. The cause was a prior row version marking runs unwritten, and an unaligned row step.
The runs summed to exactly `needed` because the rows are real; extent rows are 8-byte aligned and 1.13.0 stepped by the unaligned size.
GFSAREPLAY / GFSAPPEND are the test generator's own content markers, not filesystem metadata.
